Attack with a DIFFERENT algorithm: a single-launch, warp-per-matrix, register-resident Householder-tridiagonalization + implicit-shift QL iteration (O(n^2)/step, cubic convergence -> far fewer flops than Jacobi at n=32), warp-shuffle reductions, NO SMEM staging and NO __syncthreads (warp-synchronous), eigenvalues=diagonal after convergence, Q accumulated through the reflectors+rotations. Kill ALL Python-side overhead: preallocate outputs, in-kernel residual gate (no host gate dispatch), one launch for the whole batch. Add an in-kernel near-diagonal fast path (off-diagonal-energy check -> sorted diag as L, permutation Q). cuSOLVER's 160us at this size is ~all fixed dispatch/multi-launch overhead, so the win is minimizing OUR total launches + host ops. Route n<=48 (definitely n=32) via the router with per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback. Reuse brief-5's banked verified rotation (s=-t*c) + shared-pairing-table + in-kernel-flag gate as a starting point. Forks best 9949a990 so it stacks with all existing wins.

Validated 39/39 (test0 n=32 eig 0.25 orth 1.11 << gates). Shape0=754us vs cuSOLVER 162us (correct but slower). Geomean 48767 regresses parent 43364.

trial3: tred2 drop per-column __syncwarp + flatten lower-triangle across lanes. Shape0 604->586us marginal -- wall is occupancy+serial chain not syncs. Geomean 47858.

trial4: drop per-rotation __syncwarp in tql2 eigenvector accumulation. Shape0 586->576us marginal -- SMEM round-trip LATENCY is the wall (ncu MIO-scoreboard 40%), at 6% occupancy no warps to hide it. Geomean 47770.

Shape0 546us vs warp 576 vs cuSOLVER 162. ncu: 20 CTAs, 6.25% occupancy. Geomean 47611.

Exhaustively explored warp-per-matrix QL (+ block, twist, 2-phase variants) + parallel Sturm values + in-kernel near-diagonal fast path for shape 0 (n=32 b20). NEAR-DIAGONAL fast path WINS on structured input: 50.8us vs cuSOLVER 65.9us on a diagonal n=32 b20 (EXACT), but shape0 is DENSE so it never fires there.

ROOT CAUSE (ncu, definitive, confirms brief-5's Jacobi refutation via a DIFFERENT algorithm family): batch=20 -> at most 20 one-warp/CTA units -> 6% achieved occupancy (0.02-0.06 IPC-elapsed, Waves/SM=0.01), and EVERY per-matrix phase has serial-per-lane work (tred2 Householder columns; tql2 rotation replay; Sturm count-loop) that 20 warps cannot hide. Key isolations: (a) block QL on a TRIDIAGONAL input is ~625us == dense -> the tql2 SWEEP not tred2 is the QL floor; (b) tred2 alone ~40us; (c) 2-phase phaseB warps/CTA sweep {1,2,4,8}=221us FLAT -> phaseB (GPU-filled) is NOT the floor, phaseA (~200us, Sturm-dominated at 6% occ) is. cuSOLVER wins because its batch_parallel_jacobi<32,32,16> uses ~1024 threads/matrix (32 warps -> ~4 warps/SM across the 20 active SMs) AND Jacobi is embarrassingly parallel PER SWEEP (no serial reduction phase). The brief's premise that cuSOLVER's 160us is 'all fixed dispatch overhead' is REFUTED: 105us is genuine kernel; NOTE cuSOLVER is FLAT ~155us for b=20..128 (fixed-cost-dominated), only scaling at b>=640.
